items.titleZh: 汉密尔顿在墨西哥站获得法拉利车队首个杆位
items.summaryZh: 汉密尔顿在墨西哥站夺得个人在法拉利的首个杆位，也是车队在2026赛季的首个杆位，仅以0.009秒的优势击败了乔治·拉塞尔。队友勒克莱尔最终排名第三。
items.originalTitle: Hamilton takes his first grand prix pole for Ferrari in Mexico
detailZh: 刘易斯·汉密尔顿在墨西哥站Formula 1大奖赛中赢得了他的第一个法拉利杆位，也是车队在2026赛季的第一个杆位，在紧张的排位赛中仅以0.009秒的优势击败了乔治·罗素。
汉密尔顿在Q3的银行圈中犯了一个错误，在10号弯处错过了极限点，但在最终尝试取代罗素在领奖台顶端的位置时没有犯任何错误。
队友查尔斯·勒克莱尔在整个周末似乎都占据上风，甚至在前三个Q3的最终跑道上保持了最快时间，但他在最后一圈的飞行赛中没有显著提高，只能满足于第三名，比汉密尔顿慢0.119秒。勒克莱尔在10号弯的滑行让他付出了代价，就像之前汉密尔顿所做的那样。
41岁的汉密尔顿成为自1982年42岁的马里奥·安德雷蒂以来最年长的杆位得主，并将他自己的F1杆位记录延长至105个。
紧张的比赛尾声主要是由马克斯·维斯塔潘引起的，他在Q2中突然爆发，但红牛车队在13号弯的反复刹车问题再次出现。维斯塔潘在第一圈设立了最快的成绩，并在中间圈创造了个人最佳成绩，但随后一场巨大的烟雾锁死破坏了他的圈速，他艰难地冲过终点线，排在第四位。他在周五与利亚姆·劳森的碰撞中受到了一次降级处罚。
车手总冠军领跑者基米·安东内利排在第五位，尽管他本周有望锁定冠军，但在试图引导固执的梅赛德斯车队进入可提取速度的窗口时，他的表现似乎不如拉塞尔。
兰多·诺里斯在最后一圈退出比赛，排在第六位，领先于同样在13号弯遇到问题的伊萨克·哈德贾，他的红牛车队与维斯塔潘的情况类似。
劳森和阿尔维德·林德布拉德（劳森的处罚执行后，两人将交换位置）的红牛青训车队在中场领先，领先于皮埃尔·加斯利的阿尔派车队。
林德布拉德在Q2中设定的成绩最初是第二快的，这是一个令人惊叹的成绩，但他未能保持这种节奏进入Q3。
奥斯卡·皮亚斯蒂在Q1中看起来很有竞争力，但他在Q2中首次以令人震惊的情况退赛，因为他的麦凯轮车队队友诺里斯在这次练习中跑得最快！
皮亚斯蒂在最后一圈飞驰中未能跳出降速区，因为他比第10位的加斯利慢了三分之二秒，排在第13位。就在那个令人震惊的时刻之后，诺里斯以1分16.728秒的成绩冲过终点线，展示了麦凯轮赛车在Q2中的潜力，至少在这个练习中是这样的。
后轮抓地力不足是皮亚斯蒂的抱怨，而且他还是自2024年墨西哥站以来首次在Q3之前退赛。
尼科·胡肯伯格的奥迪车率先冲出，仅比加斯利慢了0.028秒，领先于他自己的阿尔卑斯车队队友弗朗哥·科拉平托和皮亚斯蒂。
加布里埃尔·博托莱托排名第14，领先于在最后一段出现失误的奥利·贝尔曼。卡洛斯·塞恩斯的威廉姆斯赛车在比赛中落后很多，比贝尔曼慢了0.802秒。
费尔南多·阿隆索在Q1阶段最初是最快的——诚然，在所有顶级车队都设定时间之前——当时他在赛车场部分停车，疑似出现了与ERS相关的水压问题。
他说道：“我们在Q1阶段失去了一个大好机会，”并补充道：“挫败感难以想象。”
阿隆索愤怒地敲打方向盘，最终排名跌至第18位——仍然领先于他的阿斯顿·马丁车队队友拉塞尔·斯特罗尔，后者也无法充分利用本田动力套件，排名第20位。
亚历克斯·阿隆索是Q1阶段最快的退赛者——今年与威廉姆斯车队队友卡洛斯·塞恩斯相比，落后了15-4分。
勒芒赛冠军和世界耐力锦标赛冠军里约·平川取代了“并未生病”的埃斯特班·奥康，关于这位法国人为何在周末中被淘汰的猜测愈发激烈。
平川的表现并不出彩，排名第19位，位于阿隆索和斯特罗尔之间，并且比另一位哈斯车队的队友比阿曼在另一场练习赛中慢了0.2秒。但在前两圈练习中，他仅比比阿曼慢了三十分之一，在最后一圈练习中遇到了威廉姆斯车队，这很可能削弱了他的机会。
在主场大奖赛中，塞尔吉奥·佩雷斯在公认并不艰难的凯迪拉克车队队友对抗中战胜了瓦尔特里·博塔斯，领先博塔斯七成以上。
11 尼科·胡肯伯格（奥迪）1分17.306秒（比第10名慢0.036秒）
17 阿莱克斯·阿隆索（威廉姆斯）1分18.630秒（比第16名慢0.109秒）
18 费尔南多·阿隆索（阿斯顿·马丁）慢0.278秒
detailEn: Lewis Hamilton claimed his first Ferrari pole for a Formula 1 grand prix and the team's first of the 2026 season in Mexico, beating George Russell by just 0.009 seconds in a tense qualifying session.
Hamilton had messed up his banker lap earlier in Q3, missing the apex at Turn 10, but made no mistake on his final attempt to displace Russell’s Mercedes at the top of the leaderboard.

Team-mate Charles Leclerc appeared to have the upper hand over Hamilton all weekend and even held the fastest time heading into the final Q3 runs, but couldn't improve significantly on his final flying lap and had to settle for third, 0.119s off Hamilton. It was a slide at Turn 10 that cost Leclerc, as it had Hamilton earlier.
Hamilton, 41, becomes the oldest driver to score a pole since then 42-year-old Mario Andretti in 1982, and extends his own F1 record to 105 poles.

The tense finale was mainly caused by Max Verstappen who sprang to life in Q2, but Red Bull's repeated brake issues at Turn 13 struck again. Verstappen set the fastest first sector and had a personal best in the middle sector before a huge, smoke-screen lock-up ruined the lap and he limped over the line to fourth. He has a one-place penalty for his Friday incident with Liam Lawson.

Championship leader Kimi Antonelli was fifth and while he's likely to seal the title this weekend, he's looked second best to Russell in trying to coax the recalcitrant Mercedes into a window where the pace is extractable.
Lando Norris bailed out of his final lap and starts sixth, ahead of Isack Hadjar who also had issues at Turn 13 in his Red Bull, like Verstappen.
The Racing Bulls of Lawson and Arvid Lindblad (who will swap places when Lawson’s penalty is applied) led the midfield ahead of Pierre Gasly's Alpine.
Lindblad had set a time which was initially second fastest in Q2, a show-stopping time, but failed to carry that pace through to Q3.
Oscar Piastri had looked competitive in Q1 but went out in Q2 in shock circumstances for the first time in two years, as his McLaren team-mate Norris went fastest in the session!

Piastri couldn't jump out of the drop zone on his final flying lap as he was over three tenths behind 10th placed Gasly in 13th. Just moments after that shock, Norris crossed the line with a pacesetting 1m16.728s to show what the McLaren package was capable of, at least in Q2.
No rear grip was Piastri's complaint, and he went out before Q3 for the first time since Mexico 2024.
Nico Hulkenberg's Audi was the first car out, just 0.028s off Gasly, ahead of the latter's Alpine team-mate Franco Colapinto and Piastri.
Gabriel Bortoleto took 14th, ahead of an apologetic Ollie Bearman who made a mistake in the last sector. Carlos Sainz's Williams was well out of the battle, 0.802s behind even Bearman.

Fernando Alonso was initially fastest in Q1 - admittedly before all of the top teams had set a time - when he pulled over in the stadium section with a suspected water pressure issue related to the ERS.
"We lost a big opportunity," he said after Q1, adding "frustration is beyond imagination."

Alonso had punched his steering wheel in fury and eventually dropped all the way to 18th - still ahead of Aston Martin team-mate Lance Stroll who couldn't maximise the Honda-powered package either, in 20th.
Alex Albon was the fastest Q1 casualty - 15-4 down on team-mate Carlos Sainz this year now for Williams.
Le Mans winner and World Endurance champion Ryo Hirakawa stepped in for the "not ill" Esteban Ocon as speculation intensifies as to why the Frenchman was dropped mid-weekend.

Hirakawa's time was unspectacular in 19th - between Alonso and Stroll - and a second off team-mate Bearman in the other Haas. But he was just over three tenths down on Bearman in the first two runs, encountering a Williams on his final flying lap which likely blunted his chances.
At his home grand prix, Sergio Perez won the admittedly not very tough Cadillac team-mate battle against Valtteri Bottas, over seven-tenths clear of Bottas.
11 Nico Hulkenberg (Audi) 1m17.306s (0.036s gap to 10th)
17 Alex Albon (Williams) 1m18.630s (0.109s gap to 16th)
18 Fernando Alonso (Aston Martin) +0.278s

items.originalTitle: F1 Mexico GP: Lewis Hamilton beats George Russell and Charles Leclerc to pole
detailZh: F1墨西哥大奖赛：刘易斯·汉密尔顿击败乔治·拉塞尔和查尔斯·勒克莱尔获得杆位
刘易斯·汉密尔顿在墨西哥城大奖赛上以0.009秒的优势击败乔治·拉塞尔获得杆位
刘易斯·汉密尔顿通过一场激动人心的排位赛，击败乔治·拉塞尔，为法拉利赢得了2026年F1赛季的第一个杆位
拉塞尔在阿特奥多罗·赫尔曼诺斯·罗德里格斯赛道上，通过最后一圈的冲刺从查尔斯·勒克莱尔手中夺走了临时杆位，但汉密尔顿以微弱的优势，通过第一段的略微更快成绩，以0.009秒的优势获得杆位。
汉密尔顿为车队赢得了本赛季的第一个杆位，同时也是他在法拉利的首个杆位，而勒克莱尔在最后一圈只能找到微小的进步，他比他的法拉利队友慢了0.119秒。
维斯塔潘排名第四，落后不到两十分，但将在周日的第五位发车。这位荷兰人在周五的练习赛中与利亚姆·劳森发生赛道上的争执，因此被处以一位的发车位罚分。
在一场沉闷的练习赛后，车手冠军基米·安东内利排名第五，前五名的差距只有两十分。世界冠军兰多·诺里斯的麦凯轮车队也看起来有争夺杆位的威胁，但诺里斯并没有能够完成他的第一次飞驰，然后在第二次尝试中放弃了。
愤怒的伊萨克·哈德贾在低速度的13号弯道发生事故后，为红牛车队排名第七。劳森排名第八，但将在与维斯塔潘的练习事故中降级至第九位。这使他的小红牛车队队友阿维德·林德布拉德升至第八位，而劳森将站在第五排，与阿尔皮恩的皮埃尔·加斯利并肩。
在Q2阶段，汉密尔顿和皮亚斯特里在他们的首次飞驰中遇到了一些压力，需要干净利落地完成第二次尝试才能晋级Q3。
虽然汉密尔顿在Q2中获得了第四名，成功晋级到前十名的淘汰赛，但皮亚斯特里未能效仿，澳大利亚车手在第二段的糟糕表现导致他在Esses弯道损失了近半秒的时间，由于后轮抓地力不足，他被淘汰，排在第13位，落后领跑的队友诺里斯九十分之一秒。
加斯利险些在第十位晋级，取代了奥迪的尼克·胡肯伯格。在第二节的阿尔皮纳比赛中，弗朗科·科拉平托成功保持在皮亚斯特里之前，获得第12位，而加布里埃尔·博托莱托在第14位出局。
哈斯车手奥利弗·贝尔曼无法连续完成一圈干净的赛道，由于超车限制，他失去了第二次飞驰的机会，并在第15位出局，而卡洛斯·塞恩斯是Q2中唯一的威廉姆斯车手，他获得了第15位。
Q1阶段在还剩下11分钟时因费尔南多·阿隆索的故障阿斯顿·马丁赛车而红旗暂停，西班牙人在Foro Sol竞技场因动力单元问题停车。
这对这位两届F1世界冠军来说是一次令人心碎的退出，因为这似乎是车队最具竞争力的赛道之一，阿隆索的这次表现几乎足以进入Q2。
汉密尔顿以1分17.341秒的成绩领先，阿隆索的时间未能通过测试，阿斯顿·马丁车手与威廉姆斯车手亚历克斯·阿隆的测试成绩相差一秒，阿隆索的队友塞恩斯成功晋级。
32岁的丰田WEC车手里奥·伊拉卡瓦在他的大奖赛首秀中排名第19位，取代了因伤病而缺席的哈斯车手埃斯特班·奥康。
斯特罗尔在第二辆阿斯顿·马丁中排名第20，随后是凯迪拉克车队的塞戈维亚·佩雷斯和瓦尔特里·博塔斯。博塔斯由于更换了第五台法拉利动力单元而受到网格处罚，原本就应从最后一位发车。
detailEn: F1 Mexico GP: Lewis Hamilton beats George Russell and Charles Leclerc to pole
Lewis Hamilton takes pole by 0.009s from George Russell at Formula 1's Mexico City Grand Prix
Lewis Hamilton has earned Ferrari its first pole of the 2026 Formula 1 campaign by defeating George Russell in a thrilling qualifying shootout for the Mexico Grand Prix.

Russell had taken provisional pole away from Charles Leclerc with his final run at the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez, but Hamilton responded with a marginally faster first sector to take pole by a minuscule 0.009s.

As Hamilton delivered the Scuderia's first pole of the campaign and his own first pole for Ferrari, Leclerc could only find a slight improvement on his final tour as he conceded 0.119s to his Ferrari team-mate.

Max Verstappen was fourth, just under two tenths behind, but will line up in fifth on Sunday. The Dutchman took a one-place grid penalty into qualifying for an on-track altercation with Liam Lawson during Friday practice.

After a muted session championship leader Kimi Antonelli was fifth, with the top five was covered by just two tenths. In the shape of world champion Lando Norris, McLaren also looked like a threat for pole, but Norris wasn't able to nail his first flyer and then bailed out of his second.

An irate Isack Hadjar was seventh for Red Bull after going off at the low-speed Turn 13, Red Bull's Achilles heel this weekend. Lawson was eighth but will move down to ninth for his share in the practice incident with Verstappen. That promoted his Racing Bulls team-mate Arvid Lindblad to eighth, while Lawson will line up on the fifth row alongside Alpine's Pierre Gasly.
In Q2 Hamilton and Piastri were put under some pressure when they bailed out of their first flyers, needing a clean second effort to advance to Q3.

While Hamilton booked a place in the top 10 shootout with fourth place in Q2, Piastri wasn't able to follow suit, with the Australian's horrid second sector, losing nearly half a second through the Esses due to a lack of rear grip, leaving him eliminated in 13th – nine-tenths of a second behind pacesetting team-mate Norris.
Gasly narrowly made the cut in 10th at Audi's Nico Hulkenberg's expense. In the second Alpine Franco Colapinto managed to stay ahead of Piastri to take 12th, while Gabriel Bortoleto went out in 14th.
Haas man Oliver Bearman wasn't able to string a clean lap together, losing his second flyer for track limits, and was dumped out in 15th with Carlos Sainz the only Williams in Q2 as he took 15th.
The Q1 segment was red-flagged with 11 minutes on the clock for Fernando Alonso's stricken Aston Martin as the Spaniard ground to a halt at the Foro Sol arena with a power unit issue.
It was a gut-wrenching exit for the two-time F1 world champion on what was looking like one of the team's most competitive circuits, with Alonso's only flyer almost good enough for Q2.

As Hamilton led the way with a 1m17.341s, Alonso's time didn't survive the test, with the Aston driver joined in the drop zone by Williams driver Alex Albon, who was a tenth slower than his team-mate Sainz who did make the cut.

Ryo Hirakawa was 19th on his grand prix debut, the 32-year-old Toyota WEC driver standings in for the benched Esteban Ocon at Haas. Ocon was dropped by the team without any further public explanation, though it is believed tensions between the driver and his team have hit a breaking point. Ocon has already been replaced by Ferrari junior Rafa Camara for 2027.

Lance Stroll was 20th in the second Aston Martin, followed by Cadillac duo Sergio Perez and Valtteri Bottas. Bottas had already been due to start last anyway due to a grid penalty for taking a fifth Ferrari power unit.
